result.title: Who’s right - AI optimists or pessimists? Both, says Ray Dalio
result.description:
Is AI leading us towards utopia - or its opposite? Is it fuelling a stock market bubble or will it change the world for the better?

Depending on which expert you’re listening to, it could be either. But that kind of binary thinking misses a bigger point, says hedge fund manager Ray Dalio. Throughout history, transformative technologies, from the railroad to the internet, have tended to produce bubbles, and AI is no different. How societies manage the technology, he argues, will determine how the benefits - and downsides - are shared.

Read our latest monthly economic round-up, which examines global growth and the #AI boom: https://www.weforum.org/stories/economic-growth/global-growth-resilience-and-more-top-economic-stories

result.title: How cutting emissions is future-proofing industries beyond the ‘green premium’
result.description:
Cutting the greenhouse gas emissions from heavy industry has often been framed as a cost problem: why pay more for low-emission products when the conventional versions are cheaper?
But many companies are pushing ahead, with an eye on staying competitive, securing supply chains and preparing for future markets. This episode hears from two green tech companies and a Silicon Valley investor who say low-emission technologies are already making business sense.
All three are involved in the First Movers Coalition, a World Economic Forum initiative working with companies and governments to make low-emission technologies commercially viable.

Speakers:
Jennifer Holmgren, CEO of LanzaTech
Rebecca Boudreaux, President & Chief Executive Officer, Oberon Fuels
Rajesh Swaminathan, Partner, Khosla Ventures, USA
Noam Boussidan, Programme Head, First Movers Coalition

result.title: These are the 10 most gender equal countries in the world
result.description:
The first Global Gender Gap Report was published 20 years ago. After two decades of data on gender parity, it’s clear the world is travelling in the right direction.
  
Back in 2006, the average gender gap of the 97 economies that have featured in every report was 64% closed. Today it is 69% closed - a new high-water mark. 

For the third consecutive year, a higher number of economies have reported better results. The ranking tracks 14 indicators across health, education, economic participation and politics - and of those indicators, 10 have improved since last year.

The global gender gap in educational attainment is now 97% closed - and is on course to close fully in eight years’ time. 

How wide is the gender gap in your economy? Find out in the Global Gender Gap Report 2026: https://www.weforum.org/publications/global-gender-gap-report-2026

result.title: Has AI changed how you get your first job?
result.description:
Peter Brown, Global Workforce Leader at PwC, explains to the World Economic Forum’s Kateryna Gordiychuk how AI is changing the world of #work for entry-level job-seekers.

Entry-level jobs have traditionally helped young people build the #skills they need to progress. But according to PwC research, employers are now 7 times more likely to expect candidates to arrive with 'senior-level' skills.

Listen to the full conversation on our #MeetTheLeader podcast, exploring the report Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Entry-Level Work: https://open.spotify.com/episode/3QjJhkcHLrIlr3QcPpXqoT?si=9Nk9LnFVRXCS_2Bx7rg30Q&nd=1&dlsi=f77ef1ca63cb499e
